title: Smt. Anuradha Chauhan v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; consumer relegated to section 127 appeal; limitation not to be raised if filed within two weeks; predeposit required.
headnote: The High Court treated a Rs 4.18 lakh electricity bill as a provisional assessment on a checking report under Clauses 8.1/8.2 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Holding that the consumer had not given a correct picture and that a demand notice had issued after no objections, it disposed of the writ and relegated her to an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, with a two-week window in which limitation would not be raised, subject to statutory predeposit.
facts: The petitioner claimed to run a five-room paying-guest accommodation, treated as non-commercial under a Government Order dated 8 August 1994, and to have paid electricity bills regularly. She was served a bill dated 28 October 2021 for Rs 4,18,323 without prior intimation of its computation, and later a demand notice dated 4 August 2022. Invoking writ jurisdiction, she sought to quash the demand as uninformed and contrary to the non-commercial character of paying-guest use.

holding_units.topic: relegation to section 127 after clause 8.1/8.2 demand
holding_units.holding: A bill issued on a checking report under Clauses 8.1/8.2 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a provisional assessment. Where the consumer files no objection and a demand notice follows, the High Court will not examine the demand on writ; the statutory remedy is an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. An appeal filed within two weeks of the order, with a copy of it, is to be decided without a limitation objection; the statutory predeposit must still be made.

principle_tags.application: The writ challenging the Clause 8.1/8.2 checking-report demand was disposed of by relegating the consumer to a section 127 appeal, without deciding tariff characterisation or quantum.
Limitation was not examined on the merits; the Court directed that an appeal filed within two weeks with a copy of the order shall be decided without raising limitation, subject to predeposit.

not_decided.point: Whether paying-guest accommodation is non-commercial under the Government Order dated 8 August 1994
not_decided.note: The Court did not decide the tariff characterisation; it held the petitioner had not given a correct picture of a Clause 8.1/8.2 checking-report bill.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the Rs 4,18,323 assessment and the demand notice dated 4 August 2022
not_decided.note: Quantum and computation were left to the section 127 appeal.
